overview.headline: How tiny DNA segments are copied into billions for lab study

keyPoints.point: This technique amplifies small segments of DNA for molecular analysis
keyPoints.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyPoints.point: Creator Kary Mullis was awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1993
keyPoints.quote: its creator, Kary B. Mullis, was awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1993.

keyPoints.point: Amplified DNA supports laboratory techniques including fingerprinting and diagnosis of genetic disorders
keyPoints.quote: including DNA fingerprinting, detection of bacteria or viruses (particularly AIDS), and diagnosis of genetic disorders.

keyPoints.point: Sample is heated so DNA denatures into single strands that serve as templates for synthesis
keyPoints.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.

keyPoints.point: Cycle of denaturing and synthesizing is repeated many times leading to more than one billion exact copies
keyPoints.quote: The cycle of denaturing and synthesizing new DNA is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times

keyTerms.gloss: fast technique that copies small segments of DNA by amplification
keyTerms.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: heated separation where DNA splits into single strands
keyTerms.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: enzyme that builds new strands using original templates
keyTerms.quote: Next, an enzyme called "Taq polymerase" synthesizes - builds - two new strands of DNA, using the original strands as templates.

keyTerms.gloss: machine programmed to alter temperature to allow denaturing and synthesis
keyTerms.quote: It is directed by a machine called a thermocycler,

keyTerms.gloss: laboratory identification using amplified DNA patterns for diagnosis
keyTerms.quote: including DNA fingerprinting, detection of bacteria or viruses (particularly AIDS), and diagnosis of genetic disorders.
